stem: Add and give the answer in simplest form: $\frac{{=a}}{x+{=p}}+\frac{{=b}}{x-{=q}}$ (the denominator may be left factorised).
solution: The denominators $x+{=p}$ and $x-{=q}$ have no common factor, so the L.C.M. is $(x+{=p})(x-{=q})$.
Rewrite each fraction over the L.C.M.: $\frac{{=a}(x-{=q})+{=b}(x+{=p})}{(x+{=p})(x-{=q})}$.
The result is $\frac{{=a+b}x+{=b*p-a*q}}{(x+{=p})(x-{=q})}$. The numerator has no factor in common with the denominator. The domain is $x\neq -{=p}$ and $x\neq {=q}$.
notes: No book questions supplied; parent_question_id is a placeholder. Numerator constant forced positive so it prints cleanly; no cancellation is possible (numerator at x=-p is -b(p+q), at x=q is a(p+q)).
